nodes.label: DEC-4999: Smallest-sufficient-slice execution over broad refactors
nodes.rationale: Reason: shared dirty tree with concurrent agents and governance risk. Rejected alternatives: large rewrite, opportunistic cleanup.

nodes.label: DEC-bf91: Authority-first investigation (UI → selector/state → API → handler → domain → SQL/audit → downstream)
nodes.rationale: Reason: prevents hiding governance divergence behind a frontend-only warning suppression.

nodes.label: DEC-7f14: Narrowest-relevant test suite first
nodes.rationale: Reason: cost and dirty-tree safety; expand only when behaviour, contracts or shared modules change.

nodes.label: DEC-c41a: Commercial policy configuration writes a COMPLETE policy only
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not a scenario-management subsystem: G-1 made absence fail closed, so any defaulting validator would silently reintroduce the fabricated policy G-1 removed, and an unconfigure path would let the neutral cost-build-up scenario become quotation-ready.

nodes.label: DEC-8f2d: A commercial-policy change SUPERSEDES live pricing_runs in the same D1 batch
nodes.rationale: `assertCommercialCostFreshness` only revalidates the COST snapshot, so without supersession a price computed under a deleted policy would stay current and approval-ready; every current-line/readiness query already filters superseded_at IS NULL, so no new read path or migration was needed. Runs are retained as evidence, never deleted.

nodes.label: DEC-b7e2: Fire Alarm BRAND STRATEGY layer is mandatory and sits ABOVE technical matching
nodes.rationale: In-house brands: Honeywell Farenhyt (UL/FM, total Fire Alarm system points <= 2000), Gamewell (UL/FM, > 2000), Gent by Honeywell (EN). Six-step precedence: contractually mandatory brand, standards regime, project scale/points, in-house preference, technical suitability, commercial/vendor. Reason for the layer: the previous chain jumped from project requirements to product matching, so an agent could select a technically valid brand the company could not source competitively, ignoring stock, vendor partnership and pricing position. A manufacturer merely NAMED in a specification is NOT a mandate; NOTIFIER stays TECHNICALLY_VALID_ALTERNATIVE but is not automatically PREFERRED_PROJECT_BRAND. The threshold counts total system points via the governed classifier, not raw BOQ quantity.

nodes.label: DEC-c41d: Fire Alarm pre-sales is supplier-assisted, not exhaustively in-house-resolved
nodes.rationale: Chain: BOQ + Specification + Drawings → standards/mandatory brand → preferred brand → preliminary selection → preliminary BOM → supplier RFQ → supplier detailed solution → ENGINEER REVIEW → approved BOM → price approval → costing → quotation. Reason: the real company process RFQs before detailed selection is complete, so requiring 100% internal P/N resolution first misrepresents the workflow and blocks quotation on work the supplier legitimately owns, while skipping review would launder unverified manufacturer claims into governed project state. Related: when final SLC loop distribution is unclear, compute a preliminary loop count and mark it explicitly an assumption; this does not weaken CURRENT_APPROVED_ARCHITECTURE_REQUIRED or the governed panel-sizing snapshot engine.
